title: AustralianSuper scores Moody's top credit rating
full_text:
AustralianSuper has become the first Australian superannuation fund to receive an AAA long-term issuer rating from Moody's. It has assigned a stable outlook to the rating.
The AAA rating by Moody's is the highest-quality long-term credit rating on the agency's global scale, representing the lowest level of credit risk.
AustralianSuper chief executive Paul Schroder said: "AustralianSuper is the first non-government-owned pension fund globally to receive an AAA long-term issuer rating from Moody's. This rating is good for Australia - Moody's has recognised the strength of the country's superannuation system."
Moody's said AustralianSuper's AAA issuer rating reflects its dominant franchise as Australia's largest superannuation fund and the structural benefits of Australia's mandatory, defined-contribution superannuation system.
Schroder noted the rating should make a meaningful difference to reducing the costs of investments and transactions as the fund grows its global investment footprint.
"AustralianSuper uses derivatives and other financial instruments to help manage risk and ensure access to markets in all conditions," he said.
Moody's said the fund's derivative exposures are small, at less than 1% of total assets, and are used mainly to manage risk rather than for gearing.
The ratings agency added it expects the fund to remain unleveraged, given legal restrictions on borrowing by super funds. It said the rating could be downgraded if the law changed to allow super funds to borrow and AustralianSuper took on material debt.
The issue came up earlier this year, when Chandu Bhindi, who became AustralianSuper's first chief liquidity officer in January 2025, told the Australian Financial Review that being able to issue bonds or notes would give funds another source of financing during intense market stress.
However, AustralianSuper independent chair Don Russell later used a panel to clarify the fund's position. He said it did not support structural changes that would let funds play "free and easy" with leveraging up their portfolios.
"So, no to opening up new pathways for clever funds to push the envelope, on the contrary that's what we're trying to avoid," Russell said at the time.
Russell added the fund was not looking at any tools to gear up the portfolio to improve performance.
Moody's said AustralianSuper is not immune from rising industry-wide competitive challenges.
"Despite AustralianSuper's dominant market position, the fund is not immune from rising industry-wide competitive challenges from investment platforms and self-managed superannuation funds, which offer a wider range of investment options and have seen increased inflows in recent years," Moody's said.
"There is also a growing need for the fund to increase the accessibility of advice, and to evolve its retirement product options, to meet the needs of its aging members."
